title: k8s operator: tailscale ingress sometimes tries to connect to 127.0.0.1 instead of ClusterIP, fails with "netstack: could not connect to local server at ..."
body:
### What is the issue?

I'm really not sure how to reproduce this but I've seen this a couple of times. Restarting the tailscale ingress pods seems to fix it.

I set up two services (docker-registry, and headlamp) with type ClusterIP both listening on port 80.
Both services have a tailscale ingress.
This is a test cluster with only one node, so everything is on the same node.

When trying to connect, I see errors like this in the tailscale pod:
```
2024/05/09 22:55:03 Accept: TCP{100.115.199.49:52551 > 100.77.184.113:80} 64 tcp ok
2024/05/09 22:55:03 netstack: could not connect to local server at 127.0.0.1:80: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:80: connect: connection refused
```

Restarting the tailscale ingress pod seems to fix the issue.

I'm not a kubernetes expert, but it seems supicious that tailscale is trying to connect to the service on 127.0.0.1:80 rather than using the cluster IP.


```
# kubectl get svc -A
NAMESPACE         NAME                               TYPE        CLUSTER-IP     EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)                  AGE
default           kubernetes                         ClusterIP   10.233.0.1     <none>        443/TCP                  30m
docker-registry   docker-registry                    ClusterIP   10.233.22.50   <none>        80/TCP                 17m
headlamp          headlamp                           ClusterIP   10.233.49.34   <none>        80/TCP                   27m
kube-system       coredns                            ClusterIP   10.233.0.3     <none>        53/UDP,53/TCP,9153/TCP   29m
tailscale         ts-docker-registry-ingress-4w69x   ClusterIP   None           <none>        <none>                   16m
tailscale         ts-headlamp-ingress-6mzrv          ClusterIP   None           <none>        <none>                   17m
```

```
# kubectl get ingress -A
NAMESPACE         NAME                      CLASS       HOSTS   ADDRESS                                      PORTS     AGE
docker-registry   docker-registry-ingress   tailscale   *       <redacted-host>     80, 443   36m
headlamp          headlamp-ingress          tailscale   *       <redacted-host>   80, 443   36m
```

I am able to connect to both services simultaneously using `kubectl port-forward`, so I'm pretty sure this is not an inherit limitation of my kubernetes set-up.

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

_No response_

### OS

Linux

### OS version

kubernetes

### Tailscale version

1.62.1

### Other software

calico CNI

### Bug report

BUG-893cd6c8f00a44fda54bd05672e58e601316cc21d2892024305ff3afa3f4c675-20240509231821Z-5c7d259ff6d31521

comments.body: I'm seeing this again. I tried upgradng to 1.64.2 (latest helm chart) and deleting all the pods and this time I can't figure out a way to fix it.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Restarting the kubernetes host seems to have fixed it, at least for now.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I was running into this on a cluster and restarting the proxy pods did not resolve it. I'm on kubernetes v1.30 on an Ubuntu host with tailscale v1.70 and was using Calico CNI. I was able to replicate this using minikube as well but it seems to be a configuration issue/bug. 

If I define the the port for the default backend service on the tailscale ingress using a port name only, then forwarding fails and I'm stuck with this even though my service and pod have that port name defined. 
```
2024/08/12 22:10:41 netstack: could not connect to local server at 127.0.0.1:80: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:80: connect: connection refused
```
However if I define the port using the port number only, then it all seems to work fine. Is that intended?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I would like to try to reproduce this.
Would folks be able to provide us:

- the `Ingress` and `Service` resources (including the ClusterIP if possible)
- the ingress config that the proxy has. You should be able to get it by running something like:

```
$ kubectl exec -it <ingress-proxy-pod-name> -n tailscale -- tailscale serve status
```

> However if I define the port using the port number only, then it all seems to work fine. Is that intended?

No, not intended, `Ingress` with a backend where the port is defined by name only should work (I just tested this)

Same issue here, crazy thing, but i'm also experiencing it trying to expose an argocd ingress (k3s nodes on ubuntu 24.04 hosted on contabo)

I did a test, and changed the service from ClusterIP to LoadBalancer, and guess what, i can connect to it no problem (so it's not my cluster/netwoking to be broken).

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> / # tailscale serve status
No serve config

Thank you @participant5 that would explain the erorrs. It looks like the serve config (configuration for the proxy how to route traffic to the backend) was never loaded, so we fall back routing to local server where there is nothing listening.

> notice that TS_CERT_DOMAIN is undefined

This is expected, it will be undefined in the file, it's only interpolated at config set up time.

I can't tell yet why the config is not loaded.

Would you be able to:

- check if the machine has a cert domain available, you can do so via something like `tailscale debug netmap | grep -A 2 CertDomains` on the ingress proxy `Pod`, it should show the full MagicDNS name of the proxy

- check if it works if you manually load the serve config.
You can do that from the proxy Pod:
```
$ apk add curl
$ curl --unix-socket /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock "http://local-tailscaled.sock/localapi/v0/serve-config" -X POST -d '{"TCP":{"443":{"HTTPS":<nick>}},"Web":{"${TS_CERT_DOMAIN}:443":{"Handlers":{"/":{"Proxy":"https+insecure://10.43.95.1:443/"}}}}}', just swap the `${TS_CERT_DOMAIN}` for the full MagicDNS name of the proxy
```
Curious what is `tailscale serve status` after running that last command as well as whether that actually makes the routing to backend work?


> Could it be due to the different (in this case userspace level) implementation? I have no clue of the tailscale internals, this is a late night hypothesis with no backing whatsover

It's definitely an issue specific to `Ingress`. The tun mode proxies that we spin up for `Service`s don't use netstack, so we don't hit that path there.

> I've also tried creating a LoadBalancer service with the LBclass of tailscale or annotating the existing service.

@participant4 thank you for the logs- for `Ingress`, this seems to be the same issue where the proxy backend config is not loaded, you could verify if that is the case by running `tailscale serve status` from the proxy `Pod`. If LoadBalancer `Service` is _also_ not working for you that would be a separate issue and worth opening a different issue for. I also see that you are on OpenStack, not sure if that has some limitations - the proxies we spin up for LoadBalancer `Service`s need more permissions than the `Ingress` ones.

`1.77.41` Tailscale Kubernetes operator dev Helm chart/`unstable-v1.77.41` operator image version has this change - if folks get a chance to upgrade to that version, keen to hear if the issue re-appears after that.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> I also can't expose a service directly

They will be different issues, we do not create privileged containers for `Ingress` (and generally the proxying is implemented differently for reasons).
For a Tailscale `Service` there is currently no way to avoid privilged containers, so you would need to apply `privileged` profile to `tailscale` namespace https://<redacted-host>/v1.8/kubernetes-guides/configuration/pod-security/ (I don't have Talos cluster at hand, but I think that should be all that's needed).

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@participant13 thank you once again for the detailed logs.

> Fired off the following curl commands while also tailing the proxy logs.

For a `Service` unlike the `Ingress` we don't expose port 443 to tailnet, we just proxy traffic received on any port to the same port on the cluster `Service`. I think in your case here `curl -vv <redacted-host>:9000` should have worked.

Basically `Ingress` is a mechanism for exposing a bunch of `Services` over TLS to tailnet on port 443 (L7) whereas `Service` just proxies any traffic received on any port to the same port on `Service` (L3/L4)

comments.body:
I believe this issue should have been fixed in 1.78.

It seems like there were two reasons for this not working:

- issues around writing/reading serve config from the Kubernetes Secret. This should have been fixed by caching the contents of the serve config, so that we now read from memory only https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/pull/13918
Additionally we've bumped the timeout for writes and are also now writing [events to the proxy Pod](https://tailscale.com/kb/1446/kubernetes-operator-troubleshooting#proxy-logs-and-events) so that if there are more issues related to state Secret they should be observable https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/pull/14112

- HTTPS not enabled for tailnet. In 1.78 it should be easier to discover if the Ingress is not working if HTTPS is not enabled for a tailnet. The proxies now log an error if HTTPS is not enabled and the operator does not set the Ingress's hostname unless the proxies have been able to successfully load configuration https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/pull/14171

With that I am going to close this issue.
However, if there are more issues that folks observe post-1.78, keen to hear about that
